newsitem.title: USA: Travelers/Aetna cost cuts ahead of plan.
newsitem.headline: Travelers/Aetna cost cuts ahead of plan.

text.p: Travelers Group Inc said it is ahead of its plan at Travelers/Aetna Property Casualty Corp to achieve $300 million in annual cost savings by the end of 1997.
After only nine months of operation, more than half of those targeted savings at Travelers/Aetna have been achieved, Travelers said.
Travelers has an 82 percent stake in Travelers/Aetna.
Travelers/Aetna said its personal lines business turned in strong core operating results for the quarter, due to favorable prior year loss development, primarily in the automobile bodily injury line.
The personal lines business also was helped by the continued benefit of expense reduction initiatives and strong net investment income.
Travelers/Aetna reported fourth quarter core operating earnings in the personal lines business of $98.1 million, which includes $6.6 million in catastrophe losses after taxes and reinsurance.

For the full year 1996, core operating earnings were $256.4 million, which consisted of $233.7 million from the combined operations for the last three quarters and $22.7 million from Travelers only for the first quarter.
Catastrophe losses for the full year were $58.1 million after taxes and reinsurance.

The statutory combined ratio in personal lines, on a core operating income basis, for the quarter was 95.2 percent compared with 102.5 percent in the prior quarter, reflecting the favorable loss development and lower catastrophe losses.
The ratio for the full year was 100.1 percent.
On a combined basis, total net written premiums for the fourth quarter were $674 million compared with $657 million a year ago.
For the full year, total net written premiums on a combined basis were $2.675 billion compared with $2.543 billion a year ago.
Growth in targeted automobile and homeowners markets continued, as did high retention levels, Travelers/Aetna said.
In commercial lines, fourth quarter net written premiums on a combined basis were down slightly to $1.127 billion from $1.208 billion a year ago.
For the full year, total net written premiums on a combined basis were $4.668 billion compared with $5.144 billion a year ago.
The statutory combined ratio in commercial lines for the quarter, on a core operating income basis, was 108.1 percent compared with 109.0 percent in the third quarter.
The ratio for the full year was 110.0 percent.
Core operating results continued to reflect strong net investment income and benefits from expense reduction initiatives associated with the acquisition of Aetna's property-casualty operations.
Core operating earnings were $192.5 million in the fourth and included catastrophe losses, after taxes and reinsurance, of $8.4 million.

Full year operating earnings were $633.2 million, which consisted of $574.2 million from the combined operations for the last three quarters and $59.0 million from Travelers only for the first quarter. Catastrophe losses, after taxes and reinsurance, for the full year were $31.0 million.
"Personal lines have shown good growth throughout the year," Travelers/Aetna chief executive Robert Lipp said.
"We've continued our growth in target markets, reduced exposure in catastrophe-prone areas and have seen continuing positive reserve development in the personal automobile business," he said.

"In commercial lines, the impact on earnings of reduced volume from selective underwriting and the highly competitive marketplace has been offset by greater cost efficiencies in our operations and in competitive workers' compensation managed care delivery porgrams," he said.

"At the same time, we've achieved strong customer retention rates across the agency-based lines of business," he said. Combined net written premiums for the quarter were $1.801 billion compared with $1.865 billion a year ago. Combined net written premiums for the year were $7.343 billion compared with $7.687 billion in 1995.
